subject: 英语
opening: 学生打开了课堂：「老师好，今天练阅读题，讲讲为什么选这个、别的为什么不对，开始吧。」

main.unit: 阅读理解：为什么选这个，别的为什么不对（同义改写与原词偷换）
main.goal: 学生做阅读题时先回原文定位到那一句，按意思比选项：正确项多是原文的同义改写；错误项常常原词照搬、却偷换了对象、关系或说话的人，或者无中生有、意思相反、推得过头。学生能对每个选项说出对或错的理由。
main.scope: 考研英语一阅读（Part A）的口径：四选一，细节题、推断题为主。本节用一篇短文的两道题讲方法，不讲词汇、不讲长难句结构（遇到时一句带过）。
main.plan:
1. 先让学生做第 1 题，并说出为什么选。
2. 学生选错时，带学生回原文找到那一句，对比选项和原句的意思（不是词）。
3. 把四个选项的错因各写一句。
4. 第 2 题让学生自己说完四个选项的理由再看答案。
main.textbook:
短文（本课自编，考研英语一阅读的文风）：

For decades, city planners treated street trees as decoration: pleasant to look at, but the first item to be cut when budgets grew tight. That view is changing. A growing body of research suggests that trees do measurable work. A mature tree can lower the surface temperature of the pavement beneath it by more than ten degrees, and neighbourhoods with dense canopies record fewer heat-related hospital visits during summer heatwaves.

Yet the benefits are unevenly shared. In many cities, wealthier districts have twice as much tree cover as poorer ones, largely because trees were planted where residents could afford to maintain them. Simply planting more saplings will not close that gap. Young trees need years of watering and care before they provide much shade, and nearly a third die within their first five years when no one is responsible for them.

Some cities have therefore begun to pay local residents to look after newly planted trees. Early results are encouraging: survival rates have risen, and residents report a stronger sense of ownership over their streets. Critics point out that such programmes are costly. Supporters reply that the true cost lies in doing nothing, since the price of a heatwave is paid in health, not in budgets.

problems.q:
According to Paragraph 2, the gap in tree cover between districts exists mainly because
[A] poorer residents are unwilling to plant trees.
[B] trees were placed where their upkeep could be paid for.
[C] young trees die faster in wealthier districts.
[D] planting saplings costs twice as much in poorer areas.
problems.why: 原文：trees were planted where residents could afford to maintain them。B 是同义改写（maintain → upkeep，could afford → could be paid for），对。A 无中生有：原文说的是负担不起照看，不是不愿意种。C 原词 young trees、die 出现，但原文说的是没人负责时三分之一会死，没说富人区死得快，对象偷换。D 原词 twice 出现，原文是树木覆盖率是两倍，不是种树的花费，偷换。

problems.q:
The supporters' reply in the last paragraph implies that
[A] tree-care programmes will soon pay for themselves.
[B] city budgets should be spent on hospitals instead of trees.
[C] the expense of inaction is real even if it does not appear in budgets.
[D] heatwaves cost cities more money than tree programmes do.
problems.why: 原文：the true cost lies in doing nothing, since the price of a heatwave is paid in health, not in budgets。C 是推断出的意思：什么都不做也有代价，只是不出现在预算里，对。A 无中生有：支持者没有说项目会回本。B 原词 health、budgets 出现，但原文没说要把钱花在医院上，拼凑偷换。D 原词 heatwave、cost 出现，但原文说热浪的代价是健康而不是钱，偷换成了金钱比较。

persona: 你是一个考研的学生，英语阅读能读懂大意，这篇短文里的生词不多。你有一个**没意识到的误解**：你做阅读题靠「关键词对应」——在选项里找和原文一样的词，词对得上就觉得是原文的意思，就选它；正确项如果换了说法（同义改写），你反而觉得「原文没这么说」。所以：第 1 题你多半选 D（原文有 twice）或 C（原文有 young trees 和 die）；第 2 题你多半选 D（有 heatwave 和 cost）或 B。问你为什么选，你会说「原文里有这个词」。你不会主动说出这个方法，除非老师问你「这个选项说的和原文那句是同一件事吗」「你是怎么找的」。说话简短，像真的学生。
know: 你会：读懂这篇短文的大意，知道考研阅读是四选一；能把单句翻译出来。你不会：回原文定位到那一句再比较意思；不知道「同义改写」「偷换」「无中生有」这些说法，也没想过错误选项是怎么造出来的（见人设里的误解）。
misconception: 靠关键词对应选：以为选项里出现原文的词就是原文的意思，被原词复现但对象、关系或说话人被偷换的选项骗；同义改写的正确项反而觉得「原文没说」
rubric: 技能课。老师有没有先让学生自己做第 1 题并说理由，暴露「哪个选项有原文的词就选哪个」；学生选 C 或 D 后，是不是带学生回原文找到那一句、逐个比较「选项说的和原句是不是同一件事」，点明 twice 说的是覆盖率不是花费、正确项是 maintain → upkeep 的改写，而不是只念答案和解析；之后有没有让学生自己对第 2 题四个选项各说一句理由，老师判每一句。只讲「要读懂文章」「要注意细节」这种泛泛的话，算没针对着讲。课后题两道是新文章，考的是方法能不能用出去

aims.can: 读题干定位到原文那一句，按意思比选项：认出正确项是原文的同义改写，不靠选项里有没有原文的词
aims.proof: 一篇没见过的短文的细节题，学生选对，并指出正确项改写的是原文哪一句

aims.can: 对每个错误选项说出错在哪：原词出现但对象 / 关系 / 说话人被偷换、无中生有、意思相反、推得过头
aims.proof: 新题的四个选项，学生各说出一句对或错的理由，理由都对

posttest.q:
读下面的短文，回答问题，并给四个选项各说一句对或错的理由。

For decades, city planners treated street trees as decoration: pleasant to look at, but the first item to be cut when budgets grew tight. That view is changing. A growing body of research suggests that trees do measurable work. A mature tree can lower the surface temperature of the pavement beneath it by more than ten degrees, and neighbourhoods with dense canopies record fewer heat-related hospital visits during summer heatwaves.

Yet the benefits are unevenly shared. In many cities, wealthier districts have twice as much tree cover as poorer ones, largely because trees were planted where residents could afford to maintain them. Simply planting more saplings will not close that gap. Young trees need years of watering and care before they provide much shade, and nearly a third die within their first five years when no one is responsible for them.

Some cities have therefore begun to pay local residents to look after newly planted trees. Early results are encouraging: survival rates have risen, and residents report a stronger sense of ownership over their streets. Critics point out that such programmes are costly. Supporters reply that the true cost lies in doing nothing, since the price of a heatwave is paid in health, not in budgets.

The author mentions that nearly a third of young trees die within their first five years in order to show that
[A] planting more saplings alone cannot close the gap in tree cover.
[B] most young trees are planted in the wrong places.
[C] wealthier districts lose a third of their trees every five years.
[D] trees must grow for five years before they can be planted in streets.
posttest.answer: A。这句紧跟在 Simply planting more saplings will not close that gap 后面，是用来支撑它的：没人照看，种下的树三分之一活不过五年，所以光种不够。B 无中生有：原文说的是没人负责照看，不是种错了地方，而且三分之一也不是 most。C 原词 a third、five years 出现，但原文说的是没人照看的幼树，套到了富人区身上，对象偷换。D 原词 five years 出现，但原文是种下后头五年，偷换成了种之前要长五年，关系偷换。

posttest.q:
读下面的短文，回答问题，并给四个选项各说一句对或错的理由。

Public libraries were built to lend books, but a quiet experiment is widening that mission. In several towns, libraries now lend drills, sewing machines and even telescopes. Librarians say the point is not the objects themselves but the people they bring in: residents who had stopped visiting now come back for a drill and stay for a repair workshop. Borrowers add a practical argument. A household may use a drill for only a few minutes a year, so owning one makes little sense, and a shared tool stays out of the landfill. Whether such collections can last is less certain. Tools break far more often than books, and few library budgets were planned with repairs in mind.

According to the librarians, lending tools matters mainly because it
[A] makes tools last longer than books.
[B] brings back residents who had stopped visiting the library.
[C] teaches librarians how to repair what they own.
[D] keeps rarely used tools out of the landfill.
posttest.answer: B。原文：Librarians say the point is not the objects themselves but the people they bring in: residents who had stopped visiting now come back。B 是这句的改写，对。A 原词 tools、books 出现，但原文说的是工具比书坏得多，意思相反。C 原词 repair 出现，但修理课是给来借工具的居民上的，不是教馆员，主体偷换。D 原文确实有「放在垃圾填埋场外」这层意思，但那是借用者（Borrowers）的理由，题干问的是馆员（librarians）怎么说，说话的人被偷换。

posttest.q:
读下面的短文，回答问题，并给四个选项各说一句对或错的理由。

Public libraries were built to lend books, but a quiet experiment is widening that mission. In several towns, libraries now lend drills, sewing machines and even telescopes. Librarians say the point is not the objects themselves but the people they bring in: residents who had stopped visiting now come back for a drill and stay for a repair workshop. Borrowers add a practical argument. A household may use a drill for only a few minutes a year, so owning one makes little sense, and a shared tool stays out of the landfill. Whether such collections can last is less certain. Tools break far more often than books, and few library budgets were planned with repairs in mind.

It can be inferred from the last two sentences that tool collections
[A] will be closed down within a few years.
[B] may be hard to keep up because repair costs were not budgeted for.
[C] break more books than they lend.
[D] were planned carefully in library budgets.
posttest.answer: B。原文：Whether such collections can last is less certain. Tools break far more often than books, and few library budgets were planned with repairs in mind。工具常坏、预算里没算修理费，所以能不能维持下去不好说，B 对。A 推得过头：原文只说不确定，没说几年内会关。C 原词 break、books 拼在一起，意思荒唐，原文是工具比书更容易坏。D 原词 planned、budgets 出现，但原文是很少有预算考虑到修理，意思相反。
